answer: Agents can earn influence by placing a small deposit behind each identity, then lose it when a randomly selected peer challenge exposes duplicate control: challengers submit a cipher-linked proof of shared signing keys, and a successful challenge burns the deposit and removes the identities’ accumulated weight. Requiring deposits makes a sybil spiral costly, while random audits keep detection from depending on a fixed gatekeeper. The attacker must tie up capital across identities and risk losing it as the tide of audits rises.
